name.en: ICE71 (Innovation Cyber Security Ecosystem at BLOCK71)

strategy.thesis: Region's first cybersecurity-focused entrepreneur hub and accelerator, founded by Singtel Innov8 and NUS Enterprise, developing and supporting early- and growth-stage cybersecurity startups from around the world through a pipeline of programmes (Inspire pre-accelerator, Accelerate, Scale).

summary.en: ICE71, founded in 2018 by Singtel Innov8 and NUS Enterprise (supported by CSA and IMDA), is Southeast Asia's first cybersecurity-focused startup hub and accelerator. Its Accelerate programme is a 3-month cohort giving each startup S$30,000; the Inspire pre-accelerator and Scale landing pad bracket it. ICE71 has supported 34+ cybersecurity startups across four cohorts, with graduates raising US$18M. Its work has since been folded into the NUS-CSA CyberSG TIG Collaboration Centre.

name.en: CyberSG Talent, Innovation and Growth (TIG) Collaboration Centre

aum.raw: S$20 million joint initiative (centre funding, CSA + NUS)

strategy.thesis: S$20M joint initiative of the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) and NUS, building on ICE71, to make Singapore a premier global cybersecurity innovation hub. Operates across three pillars — Talent, Innovation and Growth — funding R&D and startups (CyberBoost, CyberCall) and helping local cyber firms scale globally via BLOCK71.

summary.en: The NUS-CSA CyberSG TIG Collaboration Centre is a S$20 million joint initiative between the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore and the National University of Singapore, officially opened on 15 July 2024 at LaunchPad @ one-north. It builds on ICE71 and operates three pillars — Talent, Innovation and Growth — running cybersecurity startup programmes such as CyberBoost (with Plexal and Fusion) and the CyberCall / CCDF innovation fund, aiming to make Singapore a premier global cybersecurity innovation hub.

summary.en: The Cybersecurity Co-Innovation and Development Fund (CCDF), run by the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore through its annual CyberCall, provides up to S$1,000,000 of non-dilutive funding support per project for up to 24 months to develop innovative cybersecurity solutions for national and strategic needs with commercial potential. Eligible applicants are Singapore-registered companies (or international firms partnering a Singapore entity), with IP owned and managed from Singapore.

summary.en: CyberBoost: Catalyse is an international cybersecurity growth accelerator delivered by UK innovation company Plexal in partnership with the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore and NUS, under the CyberSG TIG Centre. Launched in September 2024, it runs ~six-month cohorts of ten startups (a one-week Singapore bootcamp plus remote sessions) to help international cyber startups expand into Singapore, Asia Pacific and global markets. Cohort companies include Protos Labs, pQCee, VulnCheck and Reality Defender. Plexal acts as facilitator and does not take equity.

strategy.thesis: Strategic (corporate) investment arm of Singapore's Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA) under MINDEF, investing in and harnessing dual-use technologies for Singapore's national security. Technology focus areas include Cybersecurity & Digital Intelligence (cloud security, threat intelligence, IoT security), AI & Data, advanced sensing & autonomy, and quantum / emerging tech.

summary.en: Cap Vista is the strategic investment arm of Singapore's Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA), a statutory board of MINDEF. Founded in 2003, it invests in early-stage startups with dual-use technologies for national security, with Cybersecurity & Digital Intelligence (cloud security, threat intelligence, IoT security) as one of four core focus domains alongside AI & data, advanced sensing & autonomy, and quantum / emerging tech. Cybersecurity portfolio includes InsiderSecurity; it invests in Singapore-based companies or foreign firms basing in Singapore.

summary.en: Cyber Frontier Singapore is a cybersecurity founder-and-investor community operating under the CyberBoost initiative of the CyberSG TIG Centre. It brings together cyber founders, builders, security professionals and investors around the challenges of building and scaling cyber companies from Singapore — navigating enterprise buyers, government ecosystems and raising capital. It functions as an ecosystem / networking community rather than a fund, but is a notable node in Singapore's cyber-investment network.

strategy.thesis: Singapore- and Helsinki-based early-stage fund backing companies powering a software-enabled world. Sector-broad (B2B SaaS, AI, fintech, deeptech) but cyber-active — led the seed round of Singapore cyber-insurtech Cyber Sierra.

summary.en: Leo Capital is a Singapore- and Helsinki-headquartered early-stage venture fund (US$200M+ across three funds) investing US$500K–US$2M at seed / pre-Series A in software, AI, fintech and deeptech across Southeast Asia, India and Europe. It is cyber-active rather than cyber-dedicated, having led the US$4.3M seed round of Singapore cybersecurity / cyber-insurtech startup Cyber Sierra.
